label: Jeffrey Nuccetelli
narrative: Nuccetelli brought the base-security side of the observational record into the congressional record. In written testimony to the House Oversight Task Force on 9 September 2025 he described serving as military police at Vandenberg Air Force Base, home of the National Missile Defense project, and receiving reports on 14 October 2003 from Boeing contractors of 'a massive, glowing red square silently hovering over two missile defense sites.' The same night, security guards reported a bright fast-moving object and witnesses described 'a massive rectangular craft, larger than a football field.' A week later a patrol reported an object over the ocean that descended and 'vanished instantly into the night sky'; in 2005 a patrol reported 'a massive triangular craft, larger than a C-130, hovering low over the main base.' Two things make this testimony operationally significant rather than anecdotal. First, he states that 'Official Air Force records documenting it are now held by AARO and the FBI' - which is a specific, checkable custody claim that FOIA can be aimed at. Second, he states one witness 'was threatened and told to keep quiet about the incident,' which is the same suppression pattern the Navy witnesses describe, applied to a strategic missile installation.
